card.name: Words just before a count or percentage
card.fires_on: The word or bracket right before a patient count, percentage or time detail in adverse-reaction text, such as a drug name, "dose reduction", "interruptions" or an opening parenthesis. It is strongest where the next thing is a number like "in 6% of patients" or "(n=9)".

modes.label: Dose action before percent
modes.description: Dose change words like reduction or interruptions, or a drug name, followed by "in X% of patients".
modes.example: Peripheral neuropathy resulted in ADCETRIS dose<< reduction>> in 6% of treated patients,

modes.label: Opening parenthesis before numbers
modes.description: An opening bracket after a drug, time or cause, which is followed by n= or a range.
modes.example: Among the 92 patients who were rechallenged with either pembrolizumab<< (>>n=3) or INLYTA

modes.label: Listed manifestation or risk factor
modes.description: A symptom or risk factor in a list that is followed by a percentage.

card.writes: It suppresses the numeric-summary words (average, median, rate-is), so it seems to steer the model away from stating averages and toward a count or percent.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a safety summary where a patient count or percentage is about to be given.
